answer: A farm running 154 keys as a result pays for 154 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the nadir declaration. Because the thread audit recomputes usage from the knoll history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 802 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
